long_biography.plain_text:
Eric Poisson made the preservation of Château de Gairaut his most enduring public project. He bought the long-abandoned Belle Époque property above Nice in 1987 and directed a sympathetic restoration with decorators Jacques Grange and Christian Benais. Together they reorganised the interiors, preserved surviving frescoes and assembled furnishings and artworks suited to the original architecture.

Poisson sold the château with its interior collections in 2000 and later moved to Southeast Asia. In Bangkok, he remained active around art and design, helping connect a travelling French artist with an exhibition at P Tendercool and contributing coral sculptures from his collection. His later cultural activity continued the collecting and preservation interests first visible at Gairaut, although his underlying business and wealth base remain private.
